🥘 Ingredients

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour, sifted
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp baking soda
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • 1 cup buttermilk, room temperature
  • 1/3 cup vegetable oil
  • 1 large egg, beaten
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1 1/2 cups fresh blueberries

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a muffin tin with paper liners or grease it lightly. This step is crucial because a hot oven helps the muffins rise quickly, creating a light, fluffy texture. Preparing your pan ahead ensures the muffins don’t stick and come out clean. Avoid skipping this or the muffins might be harder to remove and could lose their shape.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Mixing the dry ingredients thoroughly helps distribute the leavening agents evenly, which is key for uniform rising. Don’t overmix at this stage—just combine until no clumps remain to avoid dense muffins.
  3. In a separate bowl, whisk the buttermilk, vegetable oil, beaten egg, and vanilla extract until smooth. This wet mixture adds moisture and tenderness. Using room temperature buttermilk prevents the batter from curdling and helps the baking soda activate properly, giving the muffins a nice lift.
  4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir gently with a spatula. Mix just until combined; the batter should be lumpy but without streaks of flour. Overmixing develops gluten, resulting in tougher muffins, so be gentle here.
  5. Fold in the fresh blueberries carefully to avoid breaking them and turning the batter purple. Folding preserves the berries’ shape and distributes them evenly, ensuring every bite has that fruity pop. If you stir too vigorously, the batter colors and texture can be affected.
  6. Spoon the batter into the muffin tin, filling each cup about 3/4 full. This allows room for the muffins to rise without spilling over. Filling too little results in small muffins; too much causes overflow and uneven baking.
  7. Optional but recommended: sprinkle a little sugar on top of each muffin to create a sweet, crunchy crust. This adds a delightful texture contrast and a subtle sparkle that looks inviting once baked.
  8. Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through for even baking. Keep an eye on them after 20 minutes; the muffins are done when a toothpick inserted comes out clean or with just a few moist crumbs. Overbaking dries them out, so timing is key.
  9. Let the muffins cool in the pan for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack. Cooling slightly helps them set and prevents crumbly bottoms. If you try to remove them too soon, they might fall apart.

  • 4 cups thinly sliced fresh jalapeños (about 10-12 jalapeños)
  • 4 cups granulated sugar
  • 2 cups apple cider vinegar
  • 2 tablespoons mustard seeds
  • 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes
  • 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by slicing the jalapeños thinly—this helps them absorb the syrup better and ensures every bite has the right balance of heat and sweetness. Be sure to wear gloves or wash your hands thoroughly afterward because the oils can irritate your skin and eyes. Thin slices also cook evenly and maintain a bit of crunch, which is crucial for the texture of cowboy candy.
  2. Combine sugar, apple cider vinegar, mustard seeds, red pepper flakes, turmeric, and salt in a large saucepan. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally to dissolve the sugar. This hot syrup is the magic that transforms the jalapeños into candy, so make sure the sugar fully dissolves to avoid graininess.
  3. Add the sliced jalapeños to the boiling syrup and reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer. Simmer uncovered for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. This slow simmer allows the jalapeños to soften slightly while the syrup thickens and infuses with all those spicy flavors.
  4. Keep an eye on the simmering jalapeños and stir gently to avoid breaking the slices. The syrup should reduce slowly—too high heat can burn the sugar and ruin the flavor. Patience here means a perfectly balanced sweet and spicy cowboy candy with that signature crunch.
  5. Once the jalapeños are tender and the syrup has thickened, remove the pan from heat. Let the mixture cool for about 10 minutes in the pot before transferring to sterilized jars. Cooling slightly thickens the syrup further and prevents condensation inside the jars.
  6. Using a slotted spoon, pack the jalapeños evenly into clean glass jars. Pour the syrup over the top, making sure the jalapeños are fully submerged to prevent spoilage. Leaving air bubbles can affect shelf life, so tap the jars gently to release trapped air.
  7. Seal the jars with lids and let them cool to room temperature before refrigerating. The candy will continue to develop flavor over the next few days. I like to wait at least 24 hours before digging in, but it’s tempting to try it immediately!
  8. Store the cowboy candy in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. The flavors mellow and blend beautifully over time, making it taste even better after a week or two. Always use a clean spoon to avoid contamination.
  9. Serve cowboy candy as a spicy-sweet topping on burgers, grilled cheese, or cheese boards. It also works wonderfully as a snack paired with crackers or even mixed into salads for a punch of flavor. Enjoy the burst of heat and sweetness in every bite!
